FINDING_ID: R4_CONV_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector` permits non-monotone time travel updates to historical rounds via `add_round_findings(round_idx, ...)`, but only invalidates `_cumulative_classes`, not any downstream metrics already externalized. More importantly within this area, historical mutation changes the meaning of all later `kappa_set`, `kappa_rate`, `_novel_classes`, `_veto`, and `estimate_gamma` results without any guard that rounds are append-only or that recomputation consumers must discard prior decisions. In a distributed P-pass system, late-arriving findings for round `r` can retroactively change whether rounds `> r` were converged, novel, or vetoed. That makes convergence detection path-dependent and unsafe unless the caller enforces immutability, which this interface does not.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Enforce append-only round registration (`round_idx` must be new and equal to max_seen+1) or provide an explicit `recompute_from(round_idx)` API that returns invalidated downstream rounds and requires caller acknowledgment before using prior decisions. If retroactive updates are intended, store per-round version counters and expose whether previously computed convergence decisions are stale.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R4_CONV_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.68  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63  
DESCRIPTION: `kappa_set()` can decrease when duplicate support is added for an already-known issue, because the denominator sums `aggregated_severity` over cumulative equivalence classes recomputed on all findings, while the numerator sums only current-round novel class severity. Since class severity is `max` within each class, adding non-novel duplicates usually leaves the denominator unchanged and pushes `kappa_set` upward, but adding a more severe duplicate of an existing issue increases the denominator despite zero novelty. This makes convergence appear stronger simply because a known issue was restated with higher severity in a later round, not because the search space is exhausted. The metric is therefore confounded by severity escalation on old classes.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Freeze class severity at first discovery for novelty accounting, or compute denominator from cumulative novel-on-first-seen classes only. Alternative: separate “coverage stability” from “severity revision” and keep severity changes out of `kappa_set`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R4_CONV_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: `estimate_gamma()` is mathematically inconsistent with the stated reliability-growth intuition because it uses cumulative class counts `|F^(<=r)|`, which are nondecreasing by construction, rather than discovery rates over time. As implemented, if cumulative classes plateau then `gamma_hat = inf`; if they grow slowly, gamma can still look favorable regardless of per-round stabilization timing. This diagnostic is not just noisy; it does not estimate the same quantity implied by the Duane-style commentary in `kappa_rate()`, so users may interpret a bogus gamma diagnostic as corroboration of convergence behavior.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either remove `estimate_gamma()` or redefine it using a proper Duane/Crow-AMSAA style formulation based on cumulative discoveries over cumulative execution time with regression in log-log space. At minimum, rename it to a heuristic growth indicator and document that it is not a Duane gamma estimate.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R4_CONV_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.61  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57  
DESCRIPTION: `add_round_findings()` accepts any `duration` value and `kappa_rate()` silently normalizes by `max(dt, 1e-10)`. Negative or zero durations therefore become tiny positive denominators, causing arbitrarily huge rates and very negative `kappa_rate`, which then gets clamped to 0 only in `kappa()`. This hides invalid input rather than rejecting it, while standalone `kappa_rate()` and any diagnostics built on it can become nonsensical. The configuration validator issue was previously noted globally, but this is a concrete convergence-area input-integrity defect.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate `duration > 0` in `add_round_findings()` and raise `ValueError` on invalid values. If missing durations are allowed, use `None` and substitute a documented default before storage, not silent numeric coercion.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R4_CONV_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.57  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.52  
DESCRIPTION: `FindingEquivalenceClass.class_id` is generated as `ec_{idx}` per computation, where `idx` depends on transient cluster iteration order. The same semantic class can receive different IDs across calls, rounds, or after historical backfill. Any downstream consumer that logs, compares, or tracks classes by `class_id` will get unstable identities. This is especially risky because the artifact presents `class_id` as a meaningful property of an equivalence class rather than a per-call local label.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make `class_id` explicit as ephemeral/local-only in docs, or generate stable IDs from canonicalized member content, e.g. hash of sorted finding IDs or normalized representative signature.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R4_CONV_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.64  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61  
DESCRIPTION: `converged()` can return `True` for an all-empty run once `round_idx >= min_rounds_for_convergence`, because `kappa_set()` becomes 1.0 on empty cumulative findings, `kappa_rate()` is 1.0 if both rounds are empty with equal rates, `kappa_adopt()` defaults to 1.0, and `_veto()` is false. This directly contradicts the validator docstring convention “not converged unless null_expected.” A prior finding noted the validator mismatch, but the underlying functional bug remains in this area: the implementation itself does not encode the stated null-run policy.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add an explicit guard in `converged()` such as `if not self.get_cumulative_classes(round_idx): return False` unless a `null_expected` flag is supplied. Update `validate_no_findings()` to assert the actual intended behavior.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R4_CONV_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.53  
FLAW_CLASS: 7  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49  
DESCRIPTION: `_novel_classes()` reconstructs `prev_findings` by flattening every member of every previous cumulative class, even though cumulative classes already encode deduplicated structure. Because cumulative classes are recomputed over all prior findings, this flattening reintroduces all duplicate raw findings and can substantially increase comparison work with no benefit to correctness under the current ANY-match novelty rule. This is a concrete avoidable inefficiency distinct from the already-noted O(n²) clustering cost.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compare against one canonical representative per prior class, or precompute token/signature representations per class/member and index them. If the novelty criterion remains “any member matches,” use per-class representative sets rather than all raw prior findings.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R4_CONV_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.55  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.60  
DESCRIPTION: The docstring for `FindingEquivalenceClass` states “Findings are equivalent if they share flaw_class and have sim >= tau_sim,” but `_finding_similarity()` and `_compute_equivalence_classes()` explicitly allow cross-class clustering when textual similarity is high. Prior reviewers caught consequences like arbitrary representative flaw class, but there is also a spec/implementation contradiction inside this area: the exposed abstraction says one thing while the detector computes another. That mismatch undermines interpretability and validator design because users cannot know whether flaw class is part of the equivalence relation or merely a bonus term.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Align the public contract with implementation. Either require same `flaw_class` for equivalence, or rewrite docs/type comments everywhere to state that flaw class is a soft similarity feature and cross-class merges are allowed.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R4_CONV_X001  
SEVERITY: 0.51  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73  
DESCRIPTION: [CROSS-COMPONENT — unverified from this scope] `ConvergenceDetector` trusts externally supplied `adoption_delta` as already normalized to the semantics of `kappa_adopt`, but no contract in this area ties it to a stable unit or source. If upstream computes delta on cumulative findings, raw findings, or allocation changes instead of adopted synthesis changes, `kappa_adopt` can dominate `min(...)` and force false non-convergence or false convergence. This area has no provenance check or schema validation for that input.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Define and enforce an `adoption_delta` contract at the API boundary: unit interval, per-round, derived from a specified object set. Consider replacing raw float input with a typed adoption summary structure validated here.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

Definitive stance: these are the additional convergence-area flaws I can verify from the provided artifact, with one cross-component risk flagged as unverified from this scope.
